reachable: Yes, on both counts, and I checked by execution rather than by reading. GRADIENT: harness.py:71-73 calls head.wrap BEFORE make_opt(net.parameters(), steps), and wrap registers the module as net.dualaddr_transport, so all 932,611 head parameters are in net.parameters() (`all head params in net.parameters(): True`). The r18 optim's Muon router only claims 2-D params with shape[0] == key_d == 64, which none of the head's tensors match (path_key is [48,256], the extractors [256,768]), so every head parameter lands in the AdamW group. I ran three real training steps with the exact genome on real standardized train embeddings: `step 1 main=9.13556 aux=2.49416` with head grad maxima `out_scale 0.001226, src_ext.weight 0.080643, dst_ext.weight 0.05214, path_key.weight 0.168637, move_gate.bias 0.063683, write_gate.weight 0.013635`, and out_scale left zero immediately (2.5e-5, 5.0e-5, 7.5e-5 after steps 1/2/3). read_gate is second-order (0.0 at step 1, 1e-6 / 4e-6 by steps 2/3) because it multiplies out_scale. The aux fires on real batches (2.47, 2.26, 2.23) and reuses the stash rather than re-running the recurrence (`mod.run calls inside aux_loss: 0`), and the main objective also flows through the injected contribution because extract_cmd_pred reads the modified tensor. SCORED PREDICTION: cups_probe._fwd_pred calls net(...) at cups_probe.py:138, which is the wrapped forward, and reads p[:, rpos] with rpos = 2*r. I built a scoring-shaped batch with a trained-scale out_scale and confirmed the head's contribution is present at rpos and moves when ONLY a mid-chain mv command embedding is re-encoded -- `head contribution at rpos (native): 0.0607`, `head contribution at rpos changes under mv re-encode: 0.0561`, `pred at rpos changes when a mv cmd changes: 0.152`. That is precisely the dependence comp_ca does not cancel. The one hole is divergence B: at the single longest window in the batch the contribution is dropped, which on the current inner and test slices is zero scored windows. STRENGTH CAVEAT, not a divergence: the aux is the mechanism's only supervision and the author's mining claim holds on the real encoder, which he could not check -- on a real 64-trajectory batch the miner selects 201 steps, 167 (83%) labelled cvar_test/cups_test with 64/64 cups_test recall, 29 'read', 4 cvar_expose, 1 cups_ctx, mined chain depths 2 to 31 (he claimed 61/69 = 88% and depths 2 to 31 on a proxy embedding). What I could NOT check is whether A_src/A_dst learn genuinely separable source/destination components, or whether path_key resolves the suffix-differing destinations after training -- both need a full run. I can only report the init state, where distinct real mv commands' source keys sit at cosine 0.50 (random 48-d pairs are 0.12), i.e. the address space starts badly smeared and the whole bet is that the aux sharpens it.
summary: The code does what the hypothesis says on every load-bearing claim I could execute. Verified by running: bit-identity at init on both the r18 arch and the plain transformer (torch.equal True, max abs diff 0.0); the original bound forward is saved first and the module holds no back-reference to net; the delta-rule recurrence, the shared path-to-key encoder, the [B,48,768] memory, and the move/write/read gates match the written equations exactly; the read is taken strictly before the step-i write and is exactly causal (corrupting obs_3 leaves reads at cmd 0..3 bit-unchanged and moves cmd 4+); the aux implements conditions (a)-(d) as described, restricts candidates to steps <= j, uses the probe's own squared-L2 decision variable, and reuses the forward pass's stash with zero extra recurrence runs; head parameters are all optimized and all receive real gradient; the contribution reaches the scored read position and varies with the mv commands alone. I additionally verified the miner on the REAL encoder, which the author explicitly could not do -- 201 mined steps on 64 real trajectories, 83% of them the cvar_test/cups_test reads, 64/64 cups_test recall, depths 2 to 31, against his proxy-embedding claim of 88% and depths 2 to 31. Measured CPU overhead 13% vs his claimed ~17%; his 290 MB activation arithmetic is correct. Four minor divergences, none of which change what the mechanism is: (1) sym_init_noise=0.02 is 96% of the extractor's own init scale, so "a copy of A_src plus small noise ... at init every command addresses a single slot" is false -- measured cos(k_src,k_dst) is 0.768 at init on real mv commands, against 0.500 between distinct commands; (2) the odd-length scoring layout makes run() drop the final command token, so the head contributes nothing at the read of the single longest window in the batch -- zero eligible windows on both the inner and test slices today, identical in both arms, but a latent bug; (3) the quoted mv observation string is the wrong renderer's; (4) the leakage probe he cites as evidence is vacuous for this head at init, though the property he claims is true and I confirmed it with the head forced load-bearing. Nothing here is a mismatch between the archived description and the archived mechanism.

divergences.claim: "A_dst is initialised as a copy of A_src plus small noise, so at init every command addresses a single slot and the src/dst split is learned." (hypothesis.txt:17)
divergences.what_the_code_does: sym_init_noise defaults to 0.02, but nn.Linear(768,256) initialises to U(-1/sqrt(768), 1/sqrt(768)), i.e. std 0.0208. The injected noise is 96% of the weight scale, so dst_ext is NOT a perturbed copy of src_ext -- it is roughly half fresh random. Measured on REAL standardized mv command embeddings, cos(k_src, k_dst) for the SAME command is 0.768 at init, while cos(k_src_i, k_src_j) for DISTINCT mv commands in the same window is 0.500. So at init a command does not address a single slot; the src/dst split is already ~half of the way to the separation between different paths, and it is random rather than learned from a symmetric start. With sym_init_noise=0.001 the same measurement gives 0.999. This changes the init prior only, not the expressivity, and the mechanism still trains.

divergences.claim: "The read is injected into the arch's own prediction at command positions as rgate(cmd_i) * (r_i * s)" (hypothesis.txt:25) -- i.e. at every command position, including the scored read.
divergences.what_the_code_does: At scoring the layout is odd-length: cups_probe.build_cups_layout builds Lmax = 2*max_r + 1. _DualAddressTransport.run sets n = L // 2 = max_r, then takes c = tok[:,0::2][:, :n], which drops the final command token at position 2*max_r, and _forward adds contrib only to cmd positions 0, 2, ..., 2*(max_r-1). So for the LONGEST window(s) in the scored batch -- exactly the rows whose read sits at position 2*max_r -- the mechanism contributes nothing at the scored read; the arch's bare prediction is scored. It affects both arms identically, so it does not bias comp_ca, and on the current slice it touches zero scored windows: inner split max r = 28 with 1 window there and 0 in the eligible slice (max r among eligible = 24); test split max r = 27 with 4 windows, 0 eligible. It is a latent structural bug that becomes material the moment the longest window is eligible. Training is unaffected (train layout is even, L = 2*maxn).

divergences.claim: "a chain of `mv <src> <dst>` steps whose observation is the string \"cwd=/ exit=0\\n\" and nothing else" (hypothesis.txt:5)
divergences.what_the_code_does: That is realenv.render_obs's format, not the format of the encoded root this eval uses. On the nocwd root the mv observation renders to "passage: exit=0\n". The property the whole design rests on -- every mv observation is byte-identical, so its embedding is one fixed vector -- holds either way, and the miner does in fact detect that cluster on the real encoder. Purely a factual slip in the write-up.

divergences.claim: "the stream's leakage probe passes (verified -- corrupting obs_3 leaves the predictions at cmd 0..3 bit-unchanged, while cmd 4+ move)" (hypothesis.txt:23) offered as evidence that the read is causal.
divergences.what_the_code_does: The causality property is TRUE, but the cited evidence cannot establish it: out_scale is exactly zero at init, so during the harness's leakage probe the head contributes literally nothing to any prediction and the probe is vacuous with respect to this head. I re-ran it with the head forced load-bearing (out_scale = 1.0, read_gate.bias = 2.0) and it still passes, and the head-internal read is exactly causal. So the claim stands on my measurement, not on the author's.
